The Nativity of the Mother of God

Icons

Feasts

The Nativity of the Mother of God

Birth of the Mother of God

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Luke 1:46–55

Philippians 2:5–11

Luke 11:27–28

King James Version · Scripture previews

The Nativity of the Theotokos celebrates Mary’s birth to Sts. Joachim and Anna. Thomas Hopko’s OCA explanation places the feast on September 8 and explicitly distinguishes its traditional narrative from the biblical record: Mary’s birth is not narrated in the New Testament.

[1] Opening two paragraphs

What is depicted

Anna reclines after childbirth; the infant Mary, Joachim, and attendants appear around her. More elaborate compositions add Joachim’s prayer and the parents’ embrace.

[2] Printed p. 1, Nativity of the Theotokos

History and tradition

Hopko describes Sts. Joachim and Anna as an elderly, childless couple awaiting the Messiah. In the traditional account, their prayer for a child is answered by Mary’s birth. He states that the story comes from apocryphal writings outside the New Testament and explains the feast as the preparation of the person who will become Christ’s Mother. The source’s theological account is distinguished from independent historical verification of each narrative detail.

[1] Paragraph on Sts. Joachim and Anna; paragraphs on historical verification and salvation

Published explanation

Hopko connects the feast with Mary’s Magnificat, Philippians 2:5–11, and Luke 11:27–28. His explanation celebrates God’s gracious action in Christ and includes the blessing of those who hear and keep God’s word. The infant in this icon is Mary; it is distinct from the Nativity of Christ.

[1] Final four paragraphs, scriptural readings and conclusion
